note: A caller-controlled digit is written into a big number object and becomes the initial value used by later arithmetic.
The absolute-value comparison selects which operand is treated as the larger addend and therefore which path reaches the low-level addition helper.

The implementation assumes the shorter operand has fully initialized digits for the requested length; the safety obligation is that the addend length and initialized storage match the low-level read size.
The result is trimmed after the low-level addition, and the uninitialized read has already occurred inside the addition helper that this call reaches.
